organizations.csv: Key quality for acct_num: 13 rows (1.3%) have no account number and there are 18 duplicate values (999 distinct over 1030 rows). organization_id is required and unique per entity, so these rows cannot load as-is; the engineer should decide at validation whether to drop, merge or assign surrogate ids. Re-sending the same id with different content is a 409 conflict in Meridian.

company_name shows 45 normalized duplicates and 11 case-variant groups; combined with the 18 duplicate acct_num values this suggests genuine duplicate accounts in the legacy CRM. Flag for de-duplication review before load rather than silently merging.

Customer rule 2 (dormant -> Inactive) is applied against last_activity_date, but the reference date is not specified; the transformation assumes '18 months before the migration run date'. Confirm with the engineer if a fixed as-of date is preferred so reruns are reproducible.

company_status is blank on 44 rows (4.3%) and organization.lifecycle_status is required; billing_country is blank on 59 rows (5.7%) and is also required. Defaults for these blanks are a validation-stage decision.

Both date columns contain future values (created_on: 4 rows up to 2027-09-03; last_activity_date: 5 rows). These are almost certainly data entry errors and will also skew the rule 2 dormancy calculation (a future last_activity_date can never be dormant).

Potential conflict with Meridian's cross-record rule 'an inactive or churned organization cannot hold a trial or active subscription': customer rule 2 can force an account to Inactive while customer rule 4 insists Strategic accounts always carry an Enterprise subscription. Any Strategic account that is dormant will fail the cross-record check when the subscription file is loaded.

Customer rule 4 (Strategic accounts always carry an Enterprise subscription, billing is wrong if it disagrees) is driven by customer_tier in this file but acts on subscription.plan in the subscriptions dataset; carry the Strategic flag forward so that mapping can apply it.

Rule 1 asks us to create or flag a primary contact from primary_contact_email, but this file has no person name and contact.first_name / contact.last_name are required. Either the contacts dataset supplies the names by matching email, or the engineer needs a fallback (e.g. derive from the email local part) before these contacts can be created. Also note 30 normalized duplicate emails across the file, and email must be unique within an organization.

annual_revenue is mapped into a USD-denominated target, but roughly 15% of rows are Canadian or Mexican accounts and no currency column exists. Customer rule 12 only covers billing amounts, not company revenue; the engineer may want to confirm whether these figures are already USD.
contacts.csv: 22 rows (1.0%) have no acct_num. contact.organization_id is required and must reference an existing organization, so those contacts cannot be loaded as-is; the engineer decides at validation whether to hold them for manual account assignment or exclude them.

Per customer rule 14 no contact is excluded for opt_out = Y (214 rows), but the opt-out signal itself is lost in Meridian. If suppression matters at go-live, it should be exported separately for the marketing tool before the legacy system is retired.

is_primary resolves to roughly 942 true values across about 1046 distinct accounts, and the platform allows at most one is_primary = true per organization. Expect accounts with multiple flagged primaries and accounts with none; the tie-break (customer rule 1: the account row's primary_contact_email wins) is applied at validation.

contact.email is required and unique within an organization: 106 values are malformed and there are 66 case-normalized duplicate addresses. Both need resolution at validation after the lower-casing transformation.

last_touch is stored in six formats with only 16.6% ISO; if it is migrated as activity.occurred_at, parsing must be format-aware (note %m/%d/%y vs %d-%b-%Y ambiguity) and 8 values are in the future (up to 2027-08-05), which will look odd against the rule 2 dormancy test.

Assumption: acct_num is the same key space as the account dataset's account number, and the organization load applies the same id derivation. If the accounts file keys organizations differently, this foreign key must be re-derived.
subscriptions.json: Rule 11 (trials older than 90 days are dead and must not be migrated) is a row-level exclusion, not a field mapping: candidate rows are the 84 with sub_status 'trialing' and/or the 27 with subscription_level 'Trial', filtered on start_dt more than 90 days before the migration cut-off date. The engineer needs an agreed cut-off date to apply it.

Rule 4 (Strategic accounts always carry an Enterprise subscription) cannot be applied from this dataset alone - it requires joining acct_num to the accounts export's customer_tier. Where the two disagree, rule 4 says billing is wrong, so plan should be forced to enterprise for those accounts; this join should be built before load.

Cross-record rule: every organization referenced by acct_num must be loaded first, and an inactive/churned organization cannot hold a trial or active subscription. Rule 2 (dormant accounts become Inactive) and rule 6 (Closed accounts are churned) can therefore reject otherwise valid active subscriptions - expect conflicts between the 611 active rows here and the account-level statuses.

acct_num is 90% unique (903 distinct over 1003 rows), so roughly 100 accounts hold more than one subscription. Nothing in the target forbids this, but confirm with the engineer that multiple concurrent subscriptions per organization is intended rather than a sign of duplicated billing records.

Data-quality items for validation, not mapping: 41 rows (4.1%) have no seat_count and 9/16 rows have no start_dt/renew_dt although all three targets are required; start_dt has 2 future values (range runs to 2027-08-01) which is unusual for a start date; renew_dt has 80 future values, which is expected. Renewal-after-start must be re-checked after date parsing, since mixed formats can produce inverted pairs.
monthly_amount has a minimum of 0; zero-MRR subscriptions (likely trials or paused accounts) will load as 0.00 unless the customer wants them excluded.
activity.csv: Cross-record rule: every value of acct_num (1000 distinct accounts) must already exist as an organization.organization_id before these 4947 activities load. The engineer should confirm the account-number formatting used when loading the organization dataset (e.g. zero padding or an 'ACCT-' prefix) and apply the identical rule here, otherwise all activity rows will fail the reference check.

Customer rule 2 (accounts with no activity in the last 18 months are dormant and must be migrated as Inactive) is computed from this dataset: the engineer should derive the latest occurred_at per acct_num and use it to set organization.lifecycle_status, rather than relying on the CRM status column. Accounts absent from activity.csv have no activity at all and are dormant by that rule.

occurred_at ranges to 2026-09-11, i.e. future-dated relative to a 2025-era migration (and back to 2016-12-07). The engineer should check with the engineer/customer whether future timestamps are legitimate scheduled or post-dated records before they feed the 18-month dormancy calculation.
activity_type contains one case-variant group ('Invoice' vs 'INVOICE', 1489 rows combined); this is an encoding artefact, not two distinct kinds.

amount holds 650 placeholder tokens and mixed numeric/float text; how blanks and unparseable values are finally treated (null vs reject) is a validation-stage decision, not a mapping one. Note that amount_usd is nullable so null is acceptable for non-financial kinds (login, note, ticket, call).
Key quality is clean: activity_id has no nulls, no duplicates, and there are no exact duplicate rows, so idempotent re-sends are not a concern for this dataset.

rows.reason: The catalog says the customer's legacy account number usually lands in organization.organization_id, and acct_num is the declared key column with 5-digit numeric values that satisfy the target pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$.
Exact name and meaning match to the required organization.name; values are company names with no competing target.

company_status carries the account lifecycle vocabulary (Active/Inactive/Prospect/Churned), which lines up with organization.lifecycle_status; subscription.status is the wrong home because this file has no subscription and 6 of 9 values fall outside that enum.

industry_code is clearly the industry classification and organization.industry is the only industry target; the letter codes map one-to-one onto the enum, but the two numeric codes need the customer to confirm their meaning.

organization.billing_region is the only state/province field in the catalog and the values (AB, GA, Colorado) are exactly state/province identifiers; this assumes the HQ state can stand in for the billing region, which is how the rest of the address data in this file is structured.

country is the account country and organization.billing_country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, required) is the only country target; the clarification below is about the meaning of 'CA' under customer rule 5, not about the choice of target.
Exact name match to organization.website and the values are URLs; only formatting work is needed.

organization.customer_since ('when the relationship started, per the customer's records') is the only organization-level date target and account creation in the legacy CRM is the closest available proxy; no other field in the file could populate it.

Rule 3 says the tier mixes two different things: Gold/Silver/Bronze are annual spend bands while Strategic is an executive designation. organization.account_priority ('how the account is treated operationally') cleanly receives 'Strategic', but whether the spend bands become priority/standard or should be preserved in organization.tags is a business decision.
Direct meaning and near-exact name match to organization.annual_revenue_usd; the values are currency amounts needing only cleanup.
Exact name match and the values are headcounts; organization.employee_count is a nullable integer.

There is no email field on organization; customer rule 1 states that the account row's primary_contact_email is authoritative for creating or flagging the primary contact, so this value belongs on a contact record linked by organization_id = acct_num.

These are internal Apex sales owner names (person-name shapes, 993 distinct); the Meridian catalog has no account-owner or user field on organization, and the contact entity is for customer-side people, not Apex staff. Nothing in the business rules asks for it to be migrated.

There is no last-activity field on organization. The value is needed as an input to customer rule 2 (dormant -> Inactive) for company_status, but whether it should also be materialised as an activity record (activity.occurred_at) requires a decision, since activity.kind and a synthetic activity_id would have to be invented.

Only 4 distinct short values across 55% of rows, so this is a coded remark rather than free prose; it could reasonably become organization.tags or an Activity of kind 'note', and which one depends on what the four values mean operationally.

Unique, non-null identifier (2279 distinct, 100% unique) on a contact dataset; values like 'CT-000102' already satisfy the contact.contact_id pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$. The deterministic match agrees and the meaning agrees.

A 5-digit account number repeated across contacts (1046 distinct over 2279 rows) is the legacy account key; the catalog states the customer's legacy account number lands in organization.organization_id, so on a contact row it is the foreign key contact.organization_id.

The target has no single full-name field; contact.first_name and contact.last_name are both required, so this one column feeds both. Mapped to first_name here with the split rule described; last_name is produced by the same rule.
Email-typed column on the contact row matching the required contact.email field by name and value shape (local@domain); the deterministic comparison agrees.
Phone-typed column on the contact row; contact.phone is the only phone target and it requires E.164 (^\+[1-9]\d{6,14}$). None of the 2117 values are E.164 today.

Free-text CRM role column maps to the contact.role enum, and customer rule 13 covers 9 of the 12 values. The target is clear, but rule 13 names CEO/Owner/Primary as 'the primary contact' while the target enum also offers 'executive', and 'Ops Manager', 'Purchasing' and 'Main' are not covered by any rule, so the enum table needs a customer decision before it is final.
Exact name and meaning match to the boolean contact.is_primary; the 8 spellings are just a vocabulary of yes/no.

The contact entity has no last-contacted or date field at all. The only plausible homes are activity.occurred_at (which would mean synthesizing one activity record per contact) or dropping the column; that is a scope decision, and customer rule 2 makes recency of activity meaningful for dormancy, so it should not be silently discarded.

Meridian has no marketing-consent or opt-out field on contact or anywhere in the catalog, so this flag has no destination. Customer rule 14 confirms opt-out is a marketing preference and not a deletion instruction, so no contact is excluded because of it and no mapping decision remains.

Dataset key, 100% populated and 100% unique, shape AAA-99999 (e.g. SUB-00415) fits the subscription_id pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ as-is; deterministic comparison also says MATCHED and the meaning agrees (one row per subscription).

Numeric legacy account number, 903 distinct over 1003 rows, i.e. the account this subscription belongs to; the catalog says the legacy account number lands in organization.organization_id, so on a subscription row it is the foreign key subscription.organization_id.

Plan/tier of the subscription; target enum is starter/professional/enterprise and the customer's rules 7 and 8 give an explicit translation table for most values. The one value the rules do not cover is 'Trial' (27 rows), which is a status, not one of the three plans.

Billing frequency maps onto subscription.billing_cycle (enum monthly/annual); 4 of the 6 source values are abbreviations or synonyms and quarterly is not supported by the target, but rule 9 tells us what to do with it.

Subscription lifecycle state; target enum is trial/active/past_due/cancelled and rule 10 covers the two values that have no direct equivalent (paused, expired). organization.lifecycle_status is the weaker candidate because these values describe the subscription, not the account.

Seat quantity maps to the required integer field subscription.seats; values are clean round numbers (5-250) but 253 of them are exported as strings, so a cast is needed. This field also drives rule 7's Legacy Gold split.
Subscription start date maps directly to the required subscription.start_date; only 18.7% of values are already ISO so the six observed formats must be parsed.
Next renewal date maps to subscription.renewal_date (required, must be after start_date); same six mixed date formats, only 18.2% ISO.

Monthly recurring amount from the billing export; rule 12 states the export amounts are monthly regardless of billing frequency and that CAD amounts migrate as-is in USD, which makes this the direct source for subscription.mrr_usd. Values are mixed types with currency decoration ('USD 60', '$40,000.00', 5100) so they need parsing.

Only USD (928) and CAD (75); there is no currency field anywhere in the target catalog and rule 12 explicitly says CAD amounts are migrated as-is into the USD field, so the column carries no information the target can store and is redundant for the migration.
Exact name match to the activity primary key; values like 'ACT-0003710' are unique (100% distinct, no nulls) and satisfy the catalog pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ as they stand.

Dataset is about activities, and the only reference field on activity is organization_id; 1000 distinct 5-digit values over 4947 rows is the shape of a legacy account number, and the catalog says the customer's legacy account number usually lands in organization.organization_id. Values match the id pattern as-is.

Name and meaning line up with activity.kind, but two of the eight observed values ('Ticket', 'Call') are outside the target enum (invoice, payment, support_ticket, login, note) and the customer's rules say nothing about activity vocabularies, so the value mapping is a business decision even though the destination field is clear.
Exact name match to the required activity.occurred_at datetime; values are timestamps with no nulls, only the encoding differs (four formats, 49.7% ISO 8601).

The only monetary field on the activity entity; 61.3% nulls is consistent with amounts existing only for invoice/payment rows (invoice + payment counts total 2563, matching the 2563 rows that carry a currency). amount_usd is nullable, so empty rows are fine.

There is no currency field on the activity entity, and the single observed value is 'USD' (2563 rows; the remaining 48.2% are blank because those rows have no amount). Customer rule 12 also says amounts migrate as-is into the USD field, so the column carries no information the target needs.
Exact name match to the optional, nullable activity.description string; short free-text-style values (max length 24) fit as they are, and the 24.5% blanks are permitted.
